_note:
FROZEN REGION CLAIMS (F2D, 2026-09-12). gen_state_registry.py merges five independent answers to 'where does this state region live and how big is it'; claims_shadow() is one of them. It read tools/data/dll_shadow_regions.json -- the differential oracle's per-site region sets -- which was deleted with the oracle at F2D.

WHAT WAS CONSUMED: exactly three fields per entry (name, addr, size). The owning-function key the entries were grouped under was DISCARDED by the reader, which never asked 'is this region shadowed' -- claims_shadow was a symbol/size source indistinguishable in role from claims_view/save/patch/hash. So only the claims are frozen here, not the grouping.

WHY THIS IS A FLAT SEQUENCE AND NOT A DEDUPLICATED SET, which is the trap a first attempt fell into: merge() is INCREMENTAL and ORDER-SENSITIVE. It re-derives its address index after every claim that opens a new region, so whether a later claim lands as its own region or is absorbed as an interior reference into an existing host depends on what came before it. Deduplicating the 1955 claims to their 317 distinct (name, addr, size) triples and sorting them changed 196 regions. This file therefore preserves the reader's exact emission ORDER and multiplicity; the committed state_regions.json is byte-identical across the change, which is what --check proves.

WHY IT COULD NOT BE DROPPED: 3 of these regions are claimed by NO other manifest (TILE_VIS_MAP_M4/M5/M6 at 0x713d1a-0x713d1c). Dropping the claim deletes them, which renumbers every later RID_* and silently invalidates the committed tables in mh_world_snapshot.gen.h and host_stock_bases.gen.h that index by that numbering.

This is the F0 frozen-inputs precedent, per the F2 ruling that a dropped census's DATA survives as a static input while its GATE goes. The measurement is finished: these are addresses and sizes in a binary that does not change. Regenerate only if the binary does.
